title: Learning Explicit Single-Cell Dynamics Using ODE Representations
claim: Prior ODE models output only a velocity to be solved numerically; ours predicts a local linear operator with an analytical solution.
layout: 2 panels, left task plot then right side-by-side contrast, color-coded equations
description: The figure has two panels. Panel (a) is a schematic plot of single-cell interpolation. The y-axis is PCA-1(z) and the x-axis marks t1, t_val and t2. Grey dots are observed cells, and orange-red arrows are predicted trajectories passing through t_val. Dashed grey curves show the underlying paths. The caption underneath defines the validation metric as the EMD between predicted and true marginals at t_val. Panel (b) sets two sub-panels side by side. On the left, 'Neural ODE predicts a velocity' is written in orange with ż = f_θ(z,t). It shows a few small grey and orange steps between z_t1 and z_t2, labeled 'numerical solve'. On the right, 'Cell-MNN predicts a linear ODE' is written in teal with ż = A_θ(z,t) z. It shows one smooth orange-red curve through teal flow lines, labeled 'analytical solve' with the matrix-exponential formula. Color distinguishes the two methods, and the eye goes first to the contrasting headings.
caption: (a) Single-cell interpolation: trajectories are evaluated by the earth mover’s distance (EMD) between predictions and the marginal distribution at a held-out time tval. (b) Like a hypernetwork, Cell-MNN predicts a linear operator Aθ(z, t) that approximates the local dynamics explicitly, whereas Neural ODEs and Flow Matching models only output a velocity.
abstract: Modeling the dynamics of cellular differentiation is fundamental to advancing the understanding and treatment of diseases associated with this process, such as cancer. With the rapid growth of single-cell datasets, this has also become a particularly promising and active domain for machine learning. Current state-of-the-art models, however, rely on computationally expensive optimal transport preprocessing and multi-stage training, while also not discovering explicit gene interactions. To address these challenges we propose Cell-Mechanistic Neural Networks (Cell-MNN), an encoder-decoder architecture whose latent representation is a locally linearized ODE governing the dynamics of cellular evolution from stem to tissue cells. Cell-MNN is fully end-to-end (besides a standard PCA pre-processing) and its ODE representation explicitly learns biologically consistent and interpretable gene interactions. Empirically, we show that Cell-MNN achieves competitive performance on single-cell benchmarks, surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in scaling to larger datasets and joint training across multiple datasets, while also learning interpretable gene interactions that we validate against the TRRUST database of gene interactions.
